prompt: A B2B payroll software company wants to grow revenue 50% in three years. The candidate's framework: (1) Company; (2) Customers; (3) Competitors. What is the flaw in this framework?

options.text: Buckets 1 and 2 overlap and should be merged
options.feedback: Company and customers are separate Cs. The issue is that the 3Cs don't give growth levers.

options.text: It is the 3Cs, which lists perspectives but no growth levers
options.feedback: Right. A growth question needs levers: more customers, more revenue per customer, new products, new segments or geographies.
A fourth C doesn't fix the problem. The structure doesn't fit.
Competitors matter. The issue is that the framework is generic.

explanation: The 3Cs describe a situation but don't organize how revenue grows. Start from levers.

extras.corrected_framework: New customers; revenue per customer (upsell, pricing); new products; new segments and geographies
